title: Pneumonia with a history of blood clots
summary: A woman admitted for pneumonia had blood clots in her leg and lungs years ago, treated and finished; they count as history, not active disease.

documents.author: P. Novak, MD (Radiology)
documents.text:
EXAM: Chest radiograph, PA and lateral
INDICATION: Cough, fever.
FINDINGS: Airspace opacity in the left lower lobe. No pleural effusion. Heart size normal. Pulmonary vasculature normal.
IMPRESSION: Left lower lobe pneumonia.

documents.author: G. Ruiz, MD (Emergency Medicine)
documents.text:
CC: Cough and fever x4 days.

HPI: 61F with HTN, hypothyroidism, HLD, GERD and history of DVT/PE presents with productive cough, fever to 38.9 C and malaise. Mild DOE. No chest pain, hemoptysis, or leg swelling. History of R femoral DVT and bilateral PE after R total knee replacement in 2022; completed anticoagulation 2023.

Vitals: T 38.7, HR 102, BP 142/86, RR 20, SpO2 95% RA.
Exam: Crackles L base. Calves symmetric, nontender, no edema. R knee well-healed scar.

Labs: WBC 14.9, Hgb 13.2, Cr 0.8, Na 139. Lactate 1.2.
CXR: LLL infiltrate.

MDM: PE considered given prior VTE, but presentation, focal exam and CXR consistent with pneumonia; no pleuritic pain, no leg findings. CTA not indicated at this time.

Assessment/Plan:
1. Community-acquired pneumonia, LLL - ceftriaxone + azithromycin. Admit.

documents.author: V. Thompson, MD (Hospital Medicine)
documents.text:
HISTORY AND PHYSICAL

HPI: See ED. Unable to keep up with oral fluids and too fatigued to manage at home.

PMH: HTN. Hypothyroidism. HLD. GERD. History of R femoral DVT and bilateral PE (provoked, post-op, 11/2022) - completed 6 months of rivaroxaban 05/2023, no recurrence, no longer on anticoagulation. S/p R TKA 11/2022.
Meds: losartan 50 mg daily, levothyroxine 100 mcg daily, pravastatin 40 mg daily, pantoprazole 40 mg daily.

Exam: T 38.2, HR 96, BP 134/80, SpO2 95% RA. Crackles LLL. No calf tenderness.

Assessment/Plan:
1. Community-acquired pneumonia, LLL - ceftriaxone 1 g + azithromycin 500 mg daily; cultures pending.
2. History of DVT/PE - completed anticoagulation 2023; no signs of current VTE. Enoxaparin 40 mg daily for prophylaxis.
3. HTN - continue losartan.
4. Hypothyroidism - levothyroxine.
5. HLD - pravastatin.
6. GERD - pantoprazole.
7. S/p R TKA - ambulating independently.

documents.author: L. Baptiste, RN
documents.text: Pt resting, cough productive of small amounts of yellow sputum. Afebrile this shift, SpO2 96% RA. Enoxaparin 40 mg SC given at 21:00 for VTE prophylaxis. Pt asked why she is getting "blood thinner shots" again; explained this is preventive while she is less active. Pt states she had clots after her knee surgery in 2022 and "finished the pills a long time ago." Calves soft, no swelling or pain. Ambulated to bathroom independently.

documents.author: V. Thompson, MD (Hospital Medicine)
documents.text:
HOSPITAL DAY 3

S: Afebrile since yesterday AM, cough improving, eating well.
O: T 36.9, HR 80, BP 128/78, SpO2 97% RA. Few crackles L base.
Labs: WBC 9.8. Blood cx no growth at 48 h.

Assessment/Plan:
1. CAP, LLL - improving; switch to cefpodoxime PO + complete azithromycin.
2. History of DVT/PE - VTE ppx continues while inpatient.
3. HTN, hypothyroidism, HLD, GERD - stable.
Plan d/c tomorrow.

documents.author: V. Thompson, MD (Hospital Medicine)
documents.text:
DISCHARGE SUMMARY
Admit: 09/21/2026   Discharge: 09/24/2026   Disposition: Home

DISCHARGE DIAGNOSES:
1. Community-acquired pneumonia, left lower lobe
2. Hypertension
3. Hypothyroidism
4. Hyperlipidemia
5. GERD
6. History of DVT/PE (2022), completed anticoagulation 2023
7. Status post right total knee arthroplasty

HOSPITAL COURSE: Treated with ceftriaxone/azithromycin, improved quickly, never needed oxygen. Transitioned to cefpodoxime to complete 5 days. Received enoxaparin prophylaxis while inpatient; no anticoagulation indicated at discharge. Encouraged ambulation.

DISCHARGE MEDICATIONS: cefpodoxime 200 mg BID x2 days; home meds unchanged.
FOLLOW-UP: PCP 1-2 weeks.

gold.explanation: The DVT and PE happened in 2022 and anticoagulation was finished in 2023, so they're personal history (Z86.711, Z86.718), not active I26/I82 codes. Prophylactic enoxaparin doesn't support Z79.01. No CC/MCC applies, so the case groups to DRG 195. A naive system that sees 'PE' and 'DVT' codes I26.99 (an MCC) and inflates it to DRG 193.
